name: isotox-pair5-6
comment: THE FIRST PAIR PALETTE (AL, 2026-08-31). Every isotoxal run so far carries at most one star family beside the regulars, so a solid whose faces include TWO DIFFERENT stars could not appear in any of them — and the first answer given for why that was acceptable was circular: "none of the six found so far is one", from a search that could not express one. There is NO mathematical ground for the exclusion, only cost. This palette removes it for one pair. ⚑ WHY PAIRS AND NOT ALL ELEVEN AT ONCE. Corner classes drive the alphabet through the point-adjacency transfer matrix: all 11 outlines together is 29 classes and ~13.1M entries against isotox-mixed's 219,868, a tables.bin near 5.3 GB, and a k=2 search of roughly 590M blocks — about 320 hours. A PAIR is 10 classes and lands under isotox-mixed, so it is CHEAPER than the run that found the first six solids. 55 pairs cover the question exhaustively; isotox-mixed already covered three of them (it carries 5*12, 8*15 and 10*24 together) and found no mixed-star solid, which is the one real datum so far. 5* and 6* first because 5*12 is the family that produced both non-prism solids — AL's U30 analogue and the genus-9 record — while every other star family has yielded only its prism.
